list.daRawPredInfo: The raw prediction value produced by the engine before any adjustments such as PAD effects, weekday corrections, or constraints are applied.
list.daPadInfo: The PAD (Prediction Adjustment Date) effect applied to this weekday. Positive values increase the prediction to account for holidays or events.
list.daWkCorrectInfo: Weekday correction factor. When enabled, historical weekday patterns are used to adjust the raw prediction for systematic day-of-week effects.

list.daUpperInfo: Upper bound of the prediction confidence interval. Represents the optimistic estimate of expected sales.
list.daPredictInfo: The final predicted value after all adjustments (PAD, weekday correction, profile correction) have been applied.
list.daCVInfo: Coefficient of variation for this outlet on this weekday. Higher values indicate more volatile sales. Used to adjust the Economic Optimal upward when variation adjustment is enabled.
list.daEOInfo: Economic Optimal delivery quantity. Balances the cost of unsold copies against the profit from sold copies to maximize net return.
list.daLatestInfo: The most recent actual delivered quantity for this weekday from the latest prediction run.
list.daCostProfitInfo: Cost per unsold unit and profit per sold unit. Used to calculate the Economic Optimal delivery quantity.
list.daConstraintsInfo: Delivery constraints applied to this outlet: fixed quantity, minimum, and maximum delivery limits.

completed.title: Completed Simulations
completed.noSimulationsHint: Run a simulation to see results here
completed.paramsNone: No parameters stored for this run
completed.overviewColSoldOutInfo: Percentage of outlet-days where all delivered copies were sold (return = 0). Higher means more outlets are selling out.
completed.overviewColIdealReturnInfo: The theoretically optimal return rate based on the cost-to-profit ratio (cost / profit × 100). Stocking above this rate wastes more on unsold copies than the margin gained from avoiding stockouts.
completed.overviewReturnRateInfo: Percentage of delivered units that were returned unsold. Lower is better. Calculated as returned / delivered × 100.
completed.overviewSellThroughInfo: Percentage of delivered units that were sold. Higher is better. Calculated as sold / delivered × 100.
completed.statsMAEInfo: Mean Absolute Error — average size of prediction errors, ignoring direction. Lower is better.
completed.statsRMSEInfo: Root Mean Squared Error — like MAE but penalises large errors more heavily. Lower is better.
completed.statsBiasInfo: Mean Error — average prediction error with sign. Positive means systematic over-prediction, negative means under-prediction. Closer to zero is better.
completed.statsMAPEInfo: Mean Absolute Percentage Error — average error as a percentage of actual values. Lower is better. Only computed over non-zero actuals.
completed.statsR2Info: Coefficient of determination — measures how well predictions explain variation in actuals. 1.0 is perfect, 0 means no better than predicting the mean, negative means worse than the mean.
completed.statsNInfo: Number of outlet-day data points used to compute the statistics.
completed.resumeDescription: Resume this simulation from where it left off. A new task will be created to complete the remaining dates.
completed.wrapUpDescription: Finalize this simulation using the data collected so far. Calculates all summary statistics without running the remaining dates.

configuration.fieldHomeDirectoryInfo: Root path on the server where customer files are located.
configuration.fieldUploadDirectoryInfo: Directory where new data files are deposited for import.
configuration.fieldUploadDirectoryStorageInfo: Archive location for already-imported upload files.
configuration.fieldForecastDirectoryInfo: Directory where forecast output files are written.
configuration.fieldForecastDirectoryStorageInfo: Archive location for previously produced forecast files.
configuration.fieldInsightsSystemPromptInfo: Custom instructions for the AI assistant. Defines how it should behave, what tone to use, and any special context about this customer's data. Leave empty to use the default prompt.
configuration.fieldInsightsSystemPromptPlaceholder: You are a sales analytics assistant for Gorm AI...
configuration.fieldInsightsHiddenPromptInfo: Additional instructions injected into the system prompt but not visible to end users. Use this for internal context, data caveats, or business rules the AI should follow silently.
configuration.fieldInsightsHiddenPromptPlaceholder: e.g. This customer uses 'sold' to mean net copies sold after returns...
configuration.fieldInsightsPredictionEngineInfo: The prediction engine used when the AI assistant runs forecasts. Choose a lighter engine for faster responses.
configuration.fieldInsightsPredictionStrategyInfo: The prediction strategy applied to insight forecasts. Controls delivery optimization, return targets, and adjustments.
configuration.fieldInsightsWorkerInfo: The Celery worker queue for insight predictions. Use a dedicated worker to avoid blocking production prediction jobs.
configuration.fieldProductionGroupInfo: The outlet group used for production runs. When set, predictions and simulations default to outlets in this group.
configuration.fieldInsightProviderInfo: The LLM provider used for AI-powered insights and chat. Controls which service handles insight generation.
configuration.fieldInsightModelInfo: The specific model variant used for insights. Different models offer different trade-offs between speed, cost, and quality.
configuration.fieldPredictionEngineInfo: The default prediction engine used when no strategy-specific override is set.
configuration.fieldMinimumInfo: The minimum delivery quantity per outlet. Predicted values below this threshold are raised to the minimum.
configuration.fieldPricePerUnitInfo: Default selling price per unit, used as a covariate for predictions when no outlet-level price is set.
configuration.fieldCostPerUnitInfo: Default cost per unit, used for economic optimal calculation when no outlet-level cost is set.
configuration.fieldProfitPerUnitInfo: Default profit per unit, used for economic optimal calculation when no outlet-level profit is set.
configuration.fieldCurrencyInfo: The currency used for displaying financial values and calculations.
configuration.fieldRoundingInfo: Method used to round the economic optimal value to a whole delivery quantity.
configuration.weekdayCorrectionInfo: When enabled, the prediction for this weekday is automatically adjusted using historical weekday patterns to account for systematic day-of-week effects.
configuration.weekdayOnlyInfo: When enabled, predictions for this weekday are trained using only historical data from the same weekday, rather than the full time series.
configuration.weekdayProfileCorrectionInfo: Applies a weekday profile correction that scales predictions based on the typical sales distribution across days of the week.
configuration.weekdayProfileCorrectionStrengthInfo: Blending factor from 0.0 (no correction) to 1.0 (full correction). Lower values apply a softer adjustment.
configuration.weekdayProfileCorrectionThresholdInfo: Minimum share divergence required before a weekday is corrected. E.g. 0.2 means only weekdays where the forecast profile differs by more than 20% from the historical profile are adjusted.
configuration.weekdayProfileCorrectionMethodInfo: Additive shifts quantiles by the same offset as the point prediction (preserves uncertainty spread). Multiplicative scales all quantiles by the same ratio (can amplify spread on low-volume days).
configuration.covariateNoSelection: Select a covariate to view details
configuration.covariateWeekdayDetailsDesc: Control which individual weekday dummies are included in the Ridge regression. Disable a day to remove its one-hot feature.
configuration.covariateHandlingInfo: How prediction engines handle external covariates (financials, PAD events, weekday features). External uses a separate Ridge regression on residuals. Native delegates to the model's built-in covariate support. None disables covariates entirely.
configuration.variationAdjustmentInfo: Adjusts the economic optimal upward for outlets and weekdays with high sales variation, protecting against stockouts on volatile days.
configuration.variationHistoryDaysInfo: Number of days of historical sales data used to calculate per-weekday variation. Capped to avoid using outdated patterns.
configuration.padBaselineWindowDaysInfo: Length of the same-weekday baseline window used to compute the PAD effect. The local baseline around each historical pad event and the recent baseline used as today's reference both use this window. Each historical bump is scaled by recent ÷ local so the pad effect tracks each outlet's sales trend.
configuration.padHistoryDaysInfo: How far back to look for historical occurrences of each pad event. Only events within this window contribute to the averaged bump, so older data can be excluded if sales patterns have shifted.
configuration.covariatePadDetailsDesc: Tune how the PAD effect is learned from historical pad-event days.
configuration.eoMethodologyInfo: How the Economic Optimal value is selected from the quantile distribution. Interpolate smoothly estimates between quantile levels. Snap selects the nearest quantile level.
configuration.eoExtrapolationInfo: Controls how the Economic Optimal handles high-margin products where the critical fractile exceeds P90. E99 extrapolates aggressively, E95 is more conservative, and Cap at E90 uses no extrapolation.
configuration.fallbackEngineInfo: When enabled, allows the system to fall back to a simpler engine if the configured AI model fails to load (e.g. finetuned to base, base to statistical). When disabled, predictions will fail with an error instead of silently using a different engine.
configuration.sectionCorrectionDesc: Automatically adjust predictions using historical weekday patterns.
configuration.sectionIsolationDesc: Train predictions using only same-weekday historical data.
configuration.sectionOpenDaysDesc: Days on which the publication is open. Closed days are excluded from simulations.
configuration.openDayInfo: When disabled, this day is treated as closed and will be skipped during simulations.
configuration.fieldFinetunedModelPathInfo: Directory where the fine-tuned model checkpoint is saved. On RunPod this is typically /models/timesfm_finetuned (mapped to the persistent volume).
configuration.fieldFinetuneSyncEveryInfo: After this many outlets have been fine-tuned, sync the checkpoint back to the production server. Lower values are safer but incur more transfer costs.
configuration.fieldSimultaneousTasksInfo: Number of tasks the worker can run in parallel. Requires a worker restart to take effect. Higher values use more RAM and CPU.
configuration.fieldPeriodicCheckInfo: How often the dashboard checks whether Celery workers are alive.
configuration.fieldAutoRestartInfo: Automatically restart the Celery worker container when it stops responding.
configuration.workerRestartRequired: Worker restart required to apply changes
configuration.optimizeSettingsDescription: Run simulations with different configuration combinations to find the most profitable settings for this customer.
configuration.optimizeModalDescription: Select which settings to optimize. Each combination will be tested via simulation.
configuration.optimizeVariationAdjustmentInfo: Tests with and without variation adjustment enabled. Variation adjustment increases the economic optimal for outlets and weekdays with high sales variation to protect against stockouts.
configuration.optimizeEoMethodologyInfo: Tests Interpolate vs Snap methodology for selecting the Economic Optimal from the quantile distribution.
configuration.optimizeEoExtrapolationInfo: Tests different extrapolation levels (E99, E95, Cap at E90, None) for handling high-margin products where the critical fractile exceeds P90.
configuration.optimizeCovariateHandlingInfo: Tests different covariate handling modes: None (no covariates), Native (model built-in), and External (separate Ridge regression).
configuration.optimizeCovariateWeekdayInfo: Tests with weekday dummies covariate on vs off.
configuration.optimizeCovariatePriceInfo: Tests with selling price covariate on vs off.
configuration.optimizeCovariatePadInfo: Tests with PAD event covariate on vs off.
configuration.optimizeWeekdayProfileCorrectionInfo: Tests with and without weekday profile correction, which scales predictions based on the typical sales distribution across days of the week.
configuration.optimizeStrategyInfo: Which prediction strategy to use for this exploration run. A strategy includes the AI model and its parameters.
configuration.optimizeDelayInfo: Number of days between the last available sales data and the prediction date. For example, 14 means predictions are made using data up to 14 days before the target date.
configuration.optimizeOutletGroupInfo: Limit the exploration to a specific outlet group instead of running against all outlets.
configuration.optimizeWorkerInfo: Pin this run to a specific Celery worker. Useful for running on a GPU-enabled server.
configuration.optimizeNoSettings: Select at least one setting to optimize
configuration.optimizeSimulationDaysInfo: How many days of historical data to simulate against. Longer periods give more reliable results but take proportionally longer.
configuration.optimizeSimulationPeriodInfo: Select the start and end dates for the simulation. Only dates with available sales data can be selected. Longer periods give more reliable results but take proportionally longer.
configuration.optimizeHistoryWindowInfo: Range of history window sizes (in days) to test for the variation adjustment calculation.
configuration.optimizeCorrectionStrengthInfo: Range of correction strength values to test. Higher values apply stronger weekday profile adjustments.
configuration.optimizeCorrectionThresholdInfo: Range of correction threshold values to test. The threshold determines when weekday profile correction kicks in.
configuration.optimizeNameInfo: An optional label for this run to help identify it in the results list.
configuration.optimizeNamePlaceholder: Optional — leave blank for default name
configuration.automatizationDescription: Run automated simulations to find optimal configuration settings for this customer.
configuration.automatizationNoDiagnostics: No diagnostics available for this run.
configuration.automatizationDeleteConfirmDescription: This will permanently delete {count} optimization run(s). This action cannot be undone.

aiModels.noModelsHint: Create your first AI model to get started.
aiModels.finetuneResetDescription: This will permanently delete all fine-tuned model weights and progress records for {name}. The next fine-tune will start from the base model.
aiModels.finetuneResetUnderstand: I understand this action cannot be undone
aiModels.finetuneContextLengthInfo: Number of historical time steps the model can look back on when making a prediction. Longer context captures more seasonal patterns but requires more memory.
aiModels.finetuneHorizonInfo: Number of future time steps the model predicts in a single forward pass. Should match your typical prediction window.
aiModels.finetuneEpochsInfo: Number of complete passes through the training data. More epochs can improve accuracy but risk overfitting on small datasets.
aiModels.finetuneEarlyStoppingMethodInfo: How the best epoch is chosen. 'Training loss' watches the loss on the data being trained on and stops when it hasn't improved for the patience window. 'Validation set' holds out the most recent slice of the period, never trains on it, and keeps the epoch that scores best on that held-out data — a better guard against overfitting on noisy series.
aiModels.finetuneValidationSplitInfo: Percentage of the most recent bars in the fine-tune period held out as a validation set (never trained on). The run keeps the epoch with the best validation loss. Typical values: 10–20%.
aiModels.finetuneEarlyStoppingPatienceInfo: Stop training a series when training loss hasn't improved for this many epochs. Set to 0 to disable. A value of 5-10 can save significant time without sacrificing quality.
aiModels.finetuneLearningRateInfo: Step size for gradient updates during training. Lower values train more slowly but produce more stable results. Typical range: 1e-5 to 1e-3.
aiModels.finetuneBatchSizeInfo: Number of training samples processed together in each gradient update. Larger batches use more GPU memory but can speed up training.
aiModels.finetuneSyncModelPathInfo: Directory where the fine-tuned model checkpoint is saved. Each engine should have its own directory. On RunPod this is typically under /models/.
aiModels.finetuneSyncEveryInfo: After this many outlets have been fine-tuned, sync the checkpoint back to the production server. Lower values are safer but incur more transfer costs.
aiModels.finetuneSyncTargetInfo: rsync destination to copy the checkpoint back to, e.g. user@host:/path/to/models/finetune/engine/. Each engine should have its own target path. Leave empty to disable sync.
aiModels.finetuneAllowNewCheckpointInfo: When disabled, fine-tuning will only resume from an existing checkpoint. If no checkpoint exists locally and cannot be pulled from the sync target, the job will fail instead of creating a new checkpoint from the base model. This prevents accidental overwrites of a trained model.
aiModels.finetuneSaneEpochsInfo: Number of initial training epochs to evaluate before deciding if an outlet's data is pathological. If the best loss hasn't dropped below the maximum MAE after this many epochs, the outlet is skipped and weights are restored.
aiModels.finetuneMaxMaeInfo: Maximum acceptable mean absolute error after the evaluation epochs. Outlets that exceed this threshold are considered pathological — their data quality issues would corrupt the shared model weights.

salesAnalysis.outletsWithIssuesTooltip: Total number of unique outlets that have at least one data quality issue (missing data, zero sales, discrepancies, or level shifts)

salesAnalysis.recurringDeliveryDesc: Calendar dates with consistently abnormal delivery quantities
salesAnalysis.nonRecurringDeliveryDesc: Individual dates with unusually high or low deliveries
salesAnalysis.zScoreTooltip: Modified Z-Score measures how far a value deviates from the median using Median Absolute Deviation (MAD). Values above 3.5 indicate significant outliers. Higher scores mean more unusual observations.
salesAnalysis.changepointsDesc: Significant shifts in the sales trend
salesAnalysis.weeklyProfileDesc: Average sales by day of week across all selected outlets
salesAnalysis.seasonalityDesc: Yearly recurring patterns detected via STL decomposition (requires 2+ years of data)
salesAnalysis.stlTooltip: Seasonal and Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) separates a time series into three components: trend (long-term direction), seasonal (recurring yearly pattern), and residual (noise). This reveals the underlying seasonal shape independent of trend changes.
salesAnalysis.seasonalityNotEnoughData: Requires at least 2 years of data to detect yearly seasonality
salesAnalysis.weekdayEffectsDesc: Outlets ranked by how strongly sales vary by day of week
salesAnalysis.fStatisticTooltip: The F-Statistic measures how strongly sales vary by day of week. Higher values mean the outlet has a more pronounced weekday pattern (e.g. strong weekday vs weekend difference). Low values indicate relatively uniform sales across all days.
salesAnalysis.divergentOutletsDesc: Outlets whose sales trend differs markedly from the aggregate
salesAnalysis.highReturnDesc: Outlets with chronically high return rates (> 15%)
salesAnalysis.soldOutDesc: Outlets frequently selling out (> 10% of days)
salesAnalysis.weekdayEfficiencyDesc: Return rate and sold-out rate by outlet and weekday
salesAnalysis.fixedAccountsDesc: Outlets with suspiciously constant sales or where sold always equals delivered
salesAnalysis.seasonalClustersDesc: Outlets grouped by similar day-of-week sales patterns
salesAnalysis.predictabilityDesc: Outlets ranked by forecast difficulty (coefficient of variation)
salesAnalysis.correlationClustersDesc: Groups of outlets whose sales move together
salesAnalysis.noCorrelation: Not enough outlets for correlation analysis
salesAnalysis.healthCoverageDesc: How much usable history exists across outlets.
salesAnalysis.healthFieldAvailabilityDesc: Percentage of sales records with optional fields populated.
salesAnalysis.healthStructuralDesc: Potential issues in outlet configuration and data.
salesAnalysis.healthDeadOutletsDesc: Outlets with no sales in 8+ weeks and no end date set.
salesAnalysis.healthDuplicatesDesc: Outlets with very similar names or addresses.
salesAnalysis.healthVolumeDistributionDesc: How concentrated sales volume is among outlets.
salesAnalysis.healthDeliveryConfigDesc: Outlets with delivery weekday records configured.
salesAnalysis.healthViabilityDesc: How many outlets qualify for each prediction engine.
salesAnalysis.healthAggregateCVDesc: Coefficient of variation of daily sales totals. High values indicate volatile, harder-to-predict demand.
salesAnalysis.cohortSequencedHelp: Outlets in each cohort are visited in a linear order (e.g. a delivery route). Enables tail-skip cascade analysis and inferred sequence ranking.
salesAnalysis.cohortSharedDriverHelp: A single driver / operator services all outlets in the cohort. Treat same-day skips as one cascading event.
salesAnalysis.cohortPickKey: Pick an outlet_info key to partition the customer's outlets into cohorts.
salesAnalysis.cohortUniverseHelp: Total number of outlets in the selected cohort(s). This is the size of the audited population, not the count of flagged outlets.
salesAnalysis.cohortWithSignalHelp: Number of cohorts with at least 5 skip events (enough activity to compute TCS) out of all cohorts analysed.
salesAnalysis.cohortWindowHelp: Date range used for skip detection. If sales data ends before the requested end date, the window is automatically trimmed back to the last available date.
salesAnalysis.cohortNoCohorts: No cohorts found for this key.
salesAnalysis.cohortComparisonDesc: One row per cohort value. Click a row to drill into per-outlet skip stats.
salesAnalysis.cohortEventCountHelp: A skip event is a single calendar date on which at least one outlet in the cohort had abnormal zero-sales (sold ≈ 0 on a day the outlet normally sells, with delivery expected).
salesAnalysis.cohortSkipObsHelp: A skipped observation is one (outlet, date) pair where sold was abnormally low. A skip event with 7 zero-sale outlets counts as 7 observations.
salesAnalysis.cohortSkipRateHelp: Pooled rate: total skipped observations divided by total expected delivery days across all outlets in the cohort.
salesAnalysis.cohortNoReportHelp: Days when a delivery was expected but no sales row exists at all. Tracked separately from skips because the meaning is ambiguous (genuine skip, data-pipeline gap, unobserved closure). Not used in the TCS analysis.
salesAnalysis.cohortTcsHelp: Tail-Concentration Score: mean Kendall tau-b between event membership and total skip count (leave-one-out). High + significant means zero-sales concentrate on the same outlets — consistent with a driver bailing on the route tail.
salesAnalysis.cohortPValueHelp: Permutation p-value for the TCS. The probability of seeing a TCS this high if skipped outlets were a random size-matched sample of the cohort. Below 0.05 means the tail concentration is statistically meaningful.
salesAnalysis.cohortTopWeekdayHelp: The weekday on which the cohort sees the most skip events. Strong concentration on one weekday hints at a specific driver or shift pattern.
salesAnalysis.cohortVerdictHelp: Tail pattern: TCS > 0.3 and p < 0.05 — skips concentrate on the same few outlets, consistent with end-of-route bailing. Skip events: enough activity to investigate but no concentration. Clean: fewer than 5 skip events.
salesAnalysis.cohortTailSignalHelp: Skips are statistically concentrated on the same outlets (TCS > 0.3, p < 0.05). Consistent with a driver bailing on the route tail.
salesAnalysis.cohortIssuesHelp: Cohort has 5+ skip events but no statistically significant concentration. Worth investigating but not a clean tail-bail pattern.
salesAnalysis.cohortCleanHelp: Fewer than 5 skip events in the detection window. Below the minimum for the TCS analysis.
salesAnalysis.cohortInferredTailDesc: Outlets disproportionately present in skip events. If the cohort is truly sequenced, these are the most likely "end of route" stops that the driver leaves first.
salesAnalysis.cohortSkipCountHelp: Number of expected delivery days where this outlet had abnormal zero-sales (sold ≈ 0 with sold-baseline meeting the minimum).
salesAnalysis.cohortAboveFloorHelp: Of this outlet's skips, how many had `delivered` above the delivery floor (default 2 — the system's minimum drop for any non-selling stop). Skips at the floor are typically uninformative (just a slow day); above-floor skips mean the driver claimed multiple papers but none sold, which is the operationally interesting case.
salesAnalysis.cohortAboveFloorPatternHelp: This outlet has at least 5 skip days, and ≥ 80% of those skips have `delivered` above the floor. That's a chronic pattern of "driver claimed real delivery, nothing sold" — worth investigating regardless of whether the route as a whole shows a tail pattern.
salesAnalysis.cohortNoReportCountHelp: Expected delivery days where this outlet has no sales row at all. Not counted as skips.
salesAnalysis.cohortExpectedDaysHelp: Number of days a delivery was expected for this outlet (open weekdays in the active period, minus PADs and sales-filter dates).
salesAnalysis.cohortTailRankHelp: Inferred position in the route from pairwise dominance: rank 1 = most likely 'last stop' (skipped most often when the driver bails early). Computed only when Sequenced is on and TCS is significant.
salesAnalysis.cohortInvestigateHelp: Generate a 3–5 sentence operations diagnosis from this cohort's statistics. Uses Claude. Token usage is tracked against the customer's quota.

pricingAnalytics.pageSubtitle: Own-price elasticity, data viability, and price-change scenarios — projected from the coefficients already fit by Ridge-capable forecast engines.
pricingAnalytics.noCustomer: Select a customer to view pricing analytics.
pricingAnalytics.windowDaysDescription: Days of history used to anchor mean price and demand.

parameters.windowDescription: Days of history used to anchor mean price, mean demand, and the within-weekday CV that drives the viability verdict. Note: the Ridge β coefficient itself is fixed by the prediction run that wrote it — this control only changes the descriptive view and the operating point ε is reported at.
parameters.engineDescription: The foundation-model engine that will run if you trigger a coefficient backfill from the Coverage card on the Elasticity tab. Each engine has its own training-history limit (max_history_length): TimesFM looks back ~1024 days, AutoGluon and Chronos-Bolt ~2048 days, Toto ~4096 days, Chronos2 and Moirai2 ~8192 days. Pick an engine whose history limit covers any price changes you need β to capture. The default reflects this customer's configured Prediction Engine (Configuration → Core).
parameters.engineHint: Engine choice does not affect the displayed numbers until a backfill is dispatched and completes. Your selection here is saved per-customer and remembered across visits.

viability.heading: Price-variation viability
viability.subheading: Does this customer's data contain enough price movement for elasticity analysis? Independent of any persisted forecast output.
viability.adequateExplain: At least half of outlets have ≥60 days of data and ≥5% within-weekday price CV. Within-weekday CV (not overall CV) is the metric Ridge identifies elasticity from — day-of-week dummies absorb the between-weekday tier.
viability.marginalExplain: At least half of outlets pass the 14-day / 2% within-weekday CV threshold — estimates will be noisy.
viability.insufficientExplain: Most outlets lack enough within-weekday price movement to estimate elasticity reliably. A weekday tier alone (e.g. Mon–Sat vs Sun) does not count — Ridge absorbs it via day-of-week dummies.
viability.deepHistorySummary: Customer's most recent price change: {date} ({daysAgo} days ago). {count} distinct prices observed across the full ladder.
viability.deepHistoryNoData: No price changes have ever been recorded in price_history for this customer.
viability.deepHistoryOutsideWindow: This is outside the {window}-day analysis window — outlets may show as “insufficient” here even though their price has actually changed. Bump the window up or run a backfill against the full history.
viability.deepHistoryWithinWindow: Within the current {window}-day analysis window, so this change is reflected in the per-outlet viability above.
viability.outletTableHint: Shown only for marginal and insufficient outlets — adequate outlets are excluded.
viability.emptyAtRisk: All outlets have adequate price variation.

elasticity.heading: Own-price elasticity
elasticity.subheading: Dimensionless sensitivity of demand to price, measured per outlet.
elasticity.coverageExplain: {covered} of {total} outlets have a usable elasticity estimate. Outlets without one have not been included in a prediction run that fit Ridge on residuals — i.e. any foundation-model engine, run with covariate handling enabled. Statistical and Custom engines never produce a coefficient.
elasticity.coverageBreakdownSubheading: How many outlets have a persisted Ridge coefficient and how many could get one with a backfill run.
elasticity.coverageWithLogHint: Coefficient fitted on log_price_per_unit (current preferred form).
elasticity.coverageWithLegacyHint: Coefficient fitted on the older level price_per_unit. Still usable; will be replaced if you re-run with the current pipeline.
elasticity.coverageMissingViableHint: No coefficient yet, but price varies enough that a Ridge-capable engine should produce a usable one.
elasticity.coverageMissingNotViableHint: No coefficient and price doesn't move enough to fit one. Backfill won't help here.
elasticity.backfillEngineHint: Any foundation-model engine fits Ridge on residuals and will populate the coefficient. Flowstate is the default; pick the engine that performs best on this customer's data.
elasticity.backfillNothingToDo: No outlets to backfill — every viable outlet already has a coefficient.
elasticity.backfillSuccess: Backfill dispatched: {count} outlets queued on {engine}. Track progress in the Tasks panel.
elasticity.noRows: No outlets match the current filter.

events.heading: Event-based elasticity
events.subheading: Each price change is treated as a single before/after experiment: a univariate forecast at the old price vs the actuals realised at the new price. ε = log(actual / forecast) / log(p_after / p_before).
events.explain: Across {detected} detected price changes, ε estimated with engine "{engine}" over a {postDays}-day post-window. Only high/medium-confidence events feed the headline median.
events.noData: No events have been built yet — click "Build events" to scan price history and compute ε.
events.buildHint: Detects every price change in price_history, then dispatches a univariate forecast per (weekday, change_date) using {engine} with a {postDays}-day post-window. Stores one ε per (event, engine, post_days).

scenarios.heading: Price-change scenarios
scenarios.subheading: Project aggregate impact across outlets with usable elasticity. Constant-elasticity (q₁ = q₀ × (1+Δ)^ε) is the default and preferred for larger adjustments; switch to linear (q₁ = q₀ × (1 + ε × Δ)) for a first-order approximation.
scenarios.projectionConstantHint: q₁ = q₀ × (1+Δ)^ε — standard economic form; better extrapolation at larger Δ.
scenarios.projectionLinearHint: q₁ = q₀ × (1 + ε × Δ) — local linear approximation; first-order Taylor of the constant form.
scenarios.adjustmentsHint: Select one or more percentage changes to evaluate.
scenarios.excludedNotice: {excluded} of {total} outlets are excluded from these totals because they lack an elasticity estimate.
scenarios.profitChartHint: Bar height is Δprofit% relative to baseline. Green = gain, red = loss.
scenarios.caveatProjectionConstant: Constant elasticity is well-behaved across moderate adjustments but still assumes the measured ε holds outside the historical price range.
scenarios.caveatProjectionLinear: The linear approximation is accurate near the current price; divergence from the constant form grows with |Δ|.
scenarios.caveatCoverage: Only outlets with a persisted Ridge coefficient contribute — widen coverage by running a Ridge-capable engine over more outlets.
scenarios.caveatProfit: Profit projections require cost data. Outlets without cost are excluded from profit totals.

recommendation.heading: Profit-maximising recommendation
recommendation.subheading: A single uniform price adjustment applied across all included outlets, picked to maximise aggregate projected profit. Bounded to ±5% outside the most-restrictive outlet's historical range.
recommendation.safeRangeHint: Constrained by the outlet whose historical price range is narrowest — wider raises would extrapolate further than 5% outside any single outlet's data.
recommendation.appliedHint: Added to the adjustment grid below.
recommendation.statusBoundaryLow: Boundary — profit rising as price falls
recommendation.statusBoundaryHighExplain: Aggregate profit was still rising at the safe ceiling. The model thinks customers may be underpriced, but extending further would extrapolate beyond the historical range. Widen the range with smaller controlled raises and re-measure.
recommendation.statusBoundaryLowExplain: Profit kept rising as price dropped — uncommon, usually a sign of wrong-sign elasticity or insufficient data. Investigate before acting.
recommendation.statusNoChangeExplain: The current price is already at or near the projected optimum within the safe range.
recommendation.statusInsufficientExplain: Not enough outlets with usable elasticity, cost, and confidence to produce a recommendation.

orchestrationsPage.noGroupsHint: Create your first group to combine multiple models

orchestrationsNewPage.name: Name
orchestrationsNewPage.descriptionPlaceholder: What is this group used for?
orchestrationsNewPage.selectModelsHelp: Choose at least 2 models to evaluate
orchestrationsNewPage.metricHelp: Optimization metric for model selection. MASE = Mean Absolute Scaled Error; Seasonal MASE scales by the seasonal naive; CRPS scores the full forecast distribution, not just the point estimate.
orchestrationsNewPage.topNHelp: Number of best-performing models to include in the orchestration group.
orchestrationsNewPage.calibrationGrainHelp: The grain the ensemble weights are learned at. Pooled combines all selected coins/pairs into one stable weight set (recommended). Per Pair learns a separate weight set for each coin/pair.
orchestrationsNewPage.calibrationUniverseHelp: The klines the ensemble is calibrated on: the quote asset, interval, and coins to score the candidate models over.
orchestrationsNewPage.quoteAssetHelp: The quote asset for the calibration klines (e.g. USDT). Options come from the klines loaded for the selected coins.
orchestrationsNewPage.intervalHelp: The kline interval used for calibration.
orchestrationsNewPage.coinsHelp: The coins to calibrate over. Leave all unchecked to use every available coin.
orchestrationsNewPage.coinsAllHint: Leave all unchecked to calibrate over all coins.
orchestrationsNewPage.runOnHelp: Calibration runs each model's inference on a worker. A model that can't run locally can be assigned to a remote server that advertises it. Models left as Local run on the default queue.
orchestrationsNewPage.modelParametersHelp: Per-model settings (e.g. model size, precision). Defaults match the AI Models page; change them here to use different settings for this group, applied at calibration and prediction.

orchestrationDetail.selectingNote: Selecting models on the chosen workers… this updates automatically when it finishes.
orchestrationDetail.reweightingNote: Reweighting the selected models… this updates automatically when it finishes.
orchestrationDetail.errorMetricHelp: The forecast error metric used to score and rank the candidate models. MASE = Mean Absolute Scaled Error; Seasonal MASE scales by the seasonal naive; CRPS scores the full forecast distribution rather than the point estimate. It only measures out-of-sample accuracy during selection.
orchestrationDetail.topNHelp: Number of best-performing models to keep in the orchestration group.
orchestrationDetail.staleNote: The saved configuration (model set, grain, metric or Top-N) differs from the one the current composition was built on. Run Initiate Orchestration to rebuild the Top-N.
orchestrationDetail.weightsAveragedNote: Weights are averaged across all pairs at this grain.
orchestrationDetail.noComposition: No composition yet. Run Initiate Orchestration to select the Top-N models and compute their weights.
orchestrationDetail.initiateDesc: Score the candidate models, keep the Top-N, and compute their blend weights.
orchestrationDetail.reinitiateDesc: Re-screen the full candidate pool and rebuild the Top-N group of models from scratch.
orchestrationDetail.reinitiateWarning: This re-screens every candidate and may change which models are in the group, replacing the current composition.
orchestrationDetail.recalibrateDesc: Keep the selected models fixed and refresh only their blend weights from recent performance.
orchestrationDetail.deleteDesc: Permanently delete this orchestration group and all associated data.
orchestrationDetail.deleteAbsoluteDescription: You are about to delete "{name}". This action cannot be undone.
orchestrationDetail.deleteUnderstand: I understand that this will permanently delete this group and all associated data.
